hero.title: Even stripes across **rolling lawns.**
hero.lede: Grand Scapes mows Linden lawns every week on a set day: mowed, trimmed, edged along walks and curbs, and blown off. The ground rolls on the high side of town and stays wet in the low spots, and the mowing plan allows for both.

local.title: High ground and low ground **in one small city.**
local.intro: The ground in Linden changes a lot for a small city. The higher ground is rolling and well drained, some of it fairly steep, while the low spots near the river are wet muck.

points.title: A slope dries out first
points.body: A slope sheds rain before it soaks in, so the grass on it thins in a dry summer. MSU Extension's tip sheet says to mow at least 3 inches high, and on a slope that extra leaf shades the soil and keeps the roots deeper.

points.title: Muck that stays soft
points.body: The muck in Linden's low spots drains very poorly and stays soft underfoot in May. A heavy mower on a soggy low spot leaves ruts that last all summer, so on a wet week the soft corner gets trimmed and the rest gets mowed.

points.title: Older lots, plenty of edges
points.body: The older lots near Bridge and Broad come with sidewalks, curbs and drives that all need a crisp edge. We edge each of those lines on every visit.

points.title: Clippings out of the drains
points.body: Clippings blown into the street end up in the city's storm drains and roadside ditches. MSU says to blow them off walks and drives back onto the lawn, and that is where ours go.

logistics.title: Mowing day in Linden.
body: Linden is about 25 minutes from our shop on Embury Road, so Linden lawns are booked on a set day of the week rather than squeezed in between stops. Each visit covers the whole job: mow, trim around beds, trees and posts, edge the walks and curb, and blow it all off.
Rob comes out for the estimate, walks the lawn, notes the slopes and the soft spots, and prices it by the week. Lots outside the city limits in Fenton Township get the same weekly plan.

When fall comes, mowing turns into [leaf removal](/leaf-removal-linden-mi/). The last cut of the year goes a little lower once the grass stops growing, which MSU Extension says cuts down on snow mold and voles over the winter.

faq.q: Who mows lawns in Linden, MI?
faq.a: Grand Scapes mows lawns in the City of Linden and the Fenton Township lots around it, every week on a set day: mowed, trimmed, edged and blown off. Call [(810) 990-3040](tel:+18109903040) or [text Rob](sms:+18109903040) for a free estimate.

faq.q: How high should a lawn be mowed in summer?
faq.a: At least 3 inches, according to MSU Extension's tip sheet. Its mowing bulletin puts current standards between 2 and 3.75 inches and notes that taller grass handles stress better. Mowing too short shrinks the root system, which hurts most on a dry slope.

faq.q: Will mowing a wet lawn hurt it?
faq.a: It can. MSU Extension says to mow when the turf is dry for a clean cut without clumps. On the muck soils in the low parts of Linden, a wet spot can also rut under a mower, so we work around it until it firms up.

faq.q: Do you mow bigger lots outside the city limits?
faq.a: Yes. We mow in Fenton Township around the city as well, and the same weekly visit applies: mow, trim, edge and blow off. If the lot runs back to a wet area or the river, show Rob where the lawn ends and the natural ground begins.
